doc.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009

title: Ron Carter and Gap Mangione in an Elmira trio
summary: Jimmy Wormworth brought Carter and Mangione to an Elmira College gig.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So some of the guys played with other groups too on occasion?

Well only the drummer. Only the drummer. Jimmy and Ronnie. They played all over the place. But then again when I had to hire somebody to get them to play with the band, they might have been from, you know, like Syracuse, from another band. And we had, and you may be familiar with these names, but we had a gig in Elmira and needed a piano and a bass player and Jimmy Wormworth was playing drums and so he said how about these © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-
guys. And I said well who are they? And he said well it’s Ron Carter on bass and Gap Mangione on piano. Chuck Mangione’s brother.

So we played at Elmira College, it was a rainy day, and when the Dixieland stopped there was a nice little trio of Carter, Mangione and Jimmy Wormworth. And of course I love that because, as I say, I did like that kind of music. There’s a little, well Gap Mangione was a fine piano player. Very esoteric.
Ron Carter must have been at Eastman at that time.
Yeah, he spent some time in Rochester.
